questions.q: What is Distant Horizons?
questions.a: Distant Horizons is a Minecraft Java Edition mod that builds and renders simplified Level of Detail terrain beyond the normal full-detail view. Longer distances still cost generation time, memory, storage and rendering resources. The official project description is at https://modrinth.com/mod/distanthorizons.

questions.q: Is Distant Horizons client-side only?
questions.a: DH can be used on the client alone, saving terrain received while exploring. The official project also supports a server/client path that sends LOD data when configured appropriately. Client-only use does not promise terrain data for unexplored areas on every server.

questions.q: Is Distant Horizons free?
questions.a: The official DH project is free and open source under LGPL-3.0-only. Use its Modrinth or linked project distribution pages; do not pay an unrelated site for a supposed required download.

questions.q: What is the difference between Distant Horizons and Voxy?
questions.a: DH and Voxy both render distant terrain using LODs. Their version, loader, graphics and shader requirements differ. The Voxy author currently specifies OpenGL 4.6 and explicit shader support; this site has not measured a performance winner. Compare exact files before choosing.

questions.q: What are the best Distant Horizons alternatives?
questions.a: Voxy is another LOD renderer. Bobby instead caches chunks received from a server and can optionally use an existing fallback world. These solve different tasks. There is no independently measured ranking on this site; select by your loader, game version and the terrain data you need.

questions.q: Does Distant Horizons work in multiplayer / on servers?
questions.a: Client-only DH can retain received terrain as you explore. A compatible DH server can separately supply LOD data. Check which path the server actually supports; more client RAM cannot force an unmodified server to deliver unexplored terrain.

questions.q: How do I install Distant Horizons on Fabric?
questions.a: Create a duplicate instance, install the matching Fabric loader and open the exact DH release page for your Minecraft version. Install the dependencies that file declares. Launch DH without shaders first; add optional Sodium and Iris only after checking their own version requirements. Do not add Fabric API or Indium merely because an old tutorial lists them.

questions.q: How do I install Distant Horizons on NeoForge / Forge?
questions.a: Forge and NeoForge are different loaders. Use the exact DH file for your game version and loader. Iris supports NeoForge 1.21.1 or newer, but not Forge; older shader stacks require separate author guidance. Launch DH alone first and do not assume an Oculus recipe applies to a current NeoForge build.

questions.q: Does Distant Horizons work with OptiFine?
questions.a: The DH project describes limited OptiFine/forward-shader behavior, so a blanket “never works” claim is too broad. For Iris-based troubleshooting, do not combine Iris with OptiFine: Iris lists that combination as incompatible. Use a version-matched, documented rendering path.

questions.q: What Minecraft versions does Distant Horizons support?
questions.a: Open the official DH file list and filter the exact Minecraft version and loader. This site links to verified release records for its installation pages; a nearby patch version or a shader project’s Minecraft badge does not establish compatibility for your whole modpack.

questions.q: How much RAM does Distant Horizons need?
questions.a: There is no universal safe heap. Use the modpack requirements, physical memory and observed workload, leaving room for the OS. The project FAQ gives workload-dependent memory examples, not a requirement for every PC. The settings tool echoes the RAM you select; it does not calculate free system memory.

questions.q: Why is my FPS low with Distant Horizons?
questions.a: Compare a stationary scene after generation settles with exploration into new terrain, then compare shaders off. Reduce generation load if exploration is the trigger. Do not change distance, heap and every rendering mod together; keep one variable per comparison.

questions.q: What are the best Distant Horizons settings for low-end PCs?
questions.a: As an editorial diagnostic baseline, try 64 LOD chunks, Low quality, 8 vanilla chunks and no shaders, then repeat the same route. These values are not a benchmark or a promise for a particular GPU. Increase gradually only if your own comparison remains responsive.

questions.q: How do I fix chunk flickering with Distant Horizons?
questions.a: Compare the same boundary without shaders and with the default resource pack first. Record dimension, time of day, exact mod builds and whether generation has finished. Flickering alone does not prove corrupt data, so do not delete a cache as the first step.

questions.q: How do I speed up LOD chunk pre-generation?
questions.a: First identify client exploration, local distant generation or a DH server supplying LODs. Use a separate test world and the installed build’s documentation before running bulk generation. More threads can reduce game responsiveness; no universal generation command or measured speed is provided here.

questions.q: Which shaders work with Distant Horizons?
questions.a: The database distinguishes explicit author DH statements from unknown exact combinations. Photon and Solas currently mention DH in their project descriptions; that is not an independently reproduced DH/Iris/shader build matrix. Read each source and the selected file’s notes before installing.

questions.q: Why do LOD chunks look different from loaded chunks with shaders?
questions.a: Near terrain and LOD terrain can use different shader paths. Compare the same viewpoint, time and resource pack; check that the chosen archive explicitly implements DH integration. A visual seam requires an exact setup and screenshot to diagnose; it is not automatically a generation failure.

questions.q: How do I enable shader support in Distant Horizons?
questions.a: Install an Iris build and matching Sodium for a supported loader and game version, then choose a shader archive whose author explicitly documents DH support. Launch DH without shaders first. Do not assume every pack has a switch called DH Support; option names depend on the archive.

questions.q: My LOD chunks disappear when I enable shaders — how do I fix this?
questions.a: Turn off only the shader and return to the same landmark. If LODs return, check the exact shader integration and renderer versions. If LODs remain absent, investigate DH activation, generation and server data before changing shader settings.

questions.q: Distant Horizons crashes on startup — what do I do?
questions.a: Duplicate the instance and confirm Minecraft, loader, Java and DH files match. Launch with DH and only its declared requirements, then add optional rendering mods one at a time. Keep the first meaningful crash-log error; a final exit code does not identify the cause.

questions.q: Why are LOD chunks not generating?
questions.a: Check that rendering and generation are enabled, and compare old saved terrain with a newly visited area. Client-only multiplayer depends on received chunks; a DH server has a separate data path. Keep shaders off while establishing which layer is failing.

questions.q: How do I fix the 'Out of Memory' error?
questions.a: Keep the exact memory error and selected heap. Check free system memory before increasing allocation, and reduce LOD workload for comparison. A Java heap error and OS memory pressure are different; do not assign nearly all physical RAM to Minecraft.

questions.q: Distant Horizons is using too much CPU — how do I fix it?
questions.a: Compare new terrain with a repeated route after generation settles. Start with the low CPU-load preset and prioritize responsiveness. High utilization while work is progressing is different from a stuck queue, and an exact thread-count optimum has not been measured here.

questions.q: Distant Horizons terrain has 'holes' or missing chunks in the distance — why?
questions.a: Compare the same location with shaders off and allow the queue to progress. If old LODs work but new terrain is missing, examine generation and terrain delivery. If all LODs disappear only with shaders, examine the rendering stack. Back up before any data reset.
